title: Ticking a core on its own is refused with the core reason
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-COREALONE-01), with description {Description-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL COREALONE PART), is tracked at {Location-A} with a Core Charge (for example $25.00), so it has a core, {Core-A}, described "Core for {Description-A}".
  • {Part-A} and {Core-A} are active.
custom_steps:
1. On the Active tab search "Core for {Description-A}".
  2. If {Core-A} has a row of its own, turn on "Deactivate parts" and tick {Core-A} only.
  3. Click "Deactivate" and confirm with "Deactivate".
  4. Read the message, then search {Part-A}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: Write down whether {Core-A} has a row of its own. If it has none, the core cannot be ticked on its own by hand: write 'not checked by hand' in the result comment and stop.
  • Step 4: The message "No parts were changed." lists the core by its number with the reason "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead."; {Core-A} and {Part-A} are both still active.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S10-R13a, S2-N3, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas 13 Oct copy: no board shows a core. Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S10-R13a: “The reasons are "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead.", "Part not found." and "Part is already in that state."”
  • PRD §8 User Feedback Summary (A core asked to change status on its own): “"A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead." | Listed as the failure reason”
  • S2-N3: “A core cannot be set active or inactive on its own. Asked to, the system refuses it with "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead."”
  • PRD §8 User Feedback Summary (Bulk change, every part failed): “"No parts were changed." | Error toast, stays until closed, lists each failed part and its reason”
